title: Seat Belts & Child Restraints
whatItIs: You must wear a seat belt if one is fitted. The driver is responsible for children under 14; passengers 14 and over for themselves.

keyFacts.text: You MUST wear a seat belt if one is fitted, unless you are exempt.
The driver MUST make sure children under 14 wear a seat belt or the right child restraint.
Children MUST use the correct child restraint until they are 12 years old or 135 cm tall, whichever comes first.
You MUST NOT put a rear-facing baby seat in a seat with an active frontal airbag.

keyFacts: Passengers aged 14 and over are responsible for wearing their own seat belts.

visual.caption: Who wears what, and who is responsible

rows: Child aged 12 or 13, or taller than 135 cm
notes: Exceptions for children apply only in a few cases, such as some taxis or an unexpected short trip.

onTheTest.question: Who is responsible for making sure a 13-year-old passenger wears a seat belt?
options: The child's parent, even if not in the car
onTheTest.why: The driver is responsible for passengers under 14. Passengers aged 14 and over are responsible for themselves.

traps: 12 years or 135 cm: whichever comes first.
Rear-facing seat in front of an active airbag: never.
A 14-year-old who doesn't wear a belt is fined, not the driver.

sources.ref: Rules 99 to 102 (Seat belts and child restraints)
